chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abu al-Abbas, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not dispute bitterly, for it will remove your glory, and do not joke excessively, for they will take liberties with you.'

key_terms.يُجْتَرَأَ عَلَيْكَ: They will take liberties with you / act boldly towards you

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between مُماراة and مُمازحة in Shia ethics and how do they affect social standing?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the delicate balance of social conduct, warning that contentious argumentation (*mumarah*) erodes one's spiritual and social prestige (*bahau*), while frivolous joking (*mumazaha*) invites disrespect and casual familiarity. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a manifestation of inner dignity, ensuring that interactions preserve mutual respect without descending into either rigidity or levity. It serves as a practical guide for maintaining *hay'a* (dignified presence) in communal settings, a key virtue in Shi'i moral theology.
